requirements.source_text: `Stable` means normative RFC and active object identifiers follow the compatibility policy for the 1.x line. An implementation claiming conformance with this revision MUST follow its normative requirements or disclose a permitted `SHOULD` deviation. It MUST NOT treat `MUST` requirements as optional because the implementation, adapter, or workflow is experimental.
A conforming implementation MUST be able to:
An implementation MUST keep these axes logically distinct:

A module MAY constrain several axes through declared applicability metadata, but it MUST NOT silently redefine another axis. For example, a platform MAY constrain length and media placement; it MUST NOT weaken a scientific evidence requirement.
- An implementation MUST NOT invent or silently strengthen material claims.
- An inference MUST NOT be presented as a verified fact.
- Missing evidence MUST NOT be converted into evidence of absence.
- Conflicting or insufficient sources MUST remain visible when they affect interpretation.
- First-person experience MUST originate from authorized author material.
- Expert authority MUST NOT be inferred from tone alone.
- An implementation MUST NOT imitate a named living author or an identifiable private person.
- Audience needs and intended outcome MUST be known or safely inferred before format conventions are optimized.
- Engagement tactics MUST NOT override meaning, evidence, safety, or consent.
- A generated image MUST NOT be presented as a photograph, screenshot, record, or other documentary evidence of a real event, person, place, product, or interface.
- A visual MUST NOT introduce unsupported data, labels, scale, causation, anatomy, features, or historical detail.
- Rights, likeness, privacy, accessibility, provenance, and mandatory disclosure MUST be handled as part of the artifact contract.
- A review MUST identify concrete affected content or assets.
- A revision MUST address findings rather than create unrelated stylistic churn.
- An artifact with an open blocker or major finding MUST NOT be labeled publication-ready.
When requirements conflict, an implementation MUST apply this order:
An explicit user preference MAY override a stylistic default or recommendation. It MUST NOT override source integrity, legitimate perspective, rights, disclosure, or a failed gate.

Within the same level, a narrower applicable requirement SHOULD override a broader one only within its declared scope. If two equal-level requirements remain incompatible, the implementation MUST record a conflict and stop the affected stage rather than choose silently.
Supports text production with `visuals.mode: none`. It MUST implement RFC-0001 through RFC-0005, required registries, context resolution, evidence classification, gates, review, and separated output.
Includes Editorial Core and visual planning or generation. It MUST implement visual requirements in RFC-0002 and RFC-0005, including provenance and accessibility handoff.
Implements RFC-0006 in addition to Editorial Core. A benchmark evaluating generated visuals MUST also conform to Editorial Visual.
A conformance statement MUST include:
An implementation MUST NOT advertise conformance as proof that every individual output is accurate, safe, lawful, accessible, or high quality.
An extension MUST NOT redefine an existing stable ID for a different meaning.

Implementations SHOULD minimize collection and retention of personal or confidential source material. They MUST respect authorization boundaries and MUST NOT place private source content into public artifacts, prompts, benchmarks, or visual assets without permission.

Security-sensitive instructions, personal data, embargoed material, copyrighted content, trademarks, and likenesses MUST retain their applicable restrictions throughout retrieval, drafting, generation, review, storage, and publication.
The pipeline is normative. A user interface MAY combine or hide stages, but a conforming implementation MUST preserve their decisions and outputs.
An implementation MAY use additional internal states. It MUST map them to these semantics in its audit record.
Before drafting, the task record MUST contain or explicitly mark unknown:
Unknown values MUST remain distinguishable from omitted optional values.
The implementation MUST:
The implementation MUST execute RFC-0004 against pinned registries.
A partial or unvalidated module set MUST NOT be used for drafting.
The implementation MUST collect only material relevant to the reader promise, evidence needs, constraints, and selected modules.
The implementation MUST distinguish user-provided material from retrieved material. It MUST NOT treat a search result snippet, model memory, or unsourced prior output as a verified source.
Every material item or planned claim MUST be classified as one of:
Material claims MUST map to a source, explicit author material, or a declared non-factual classification. An unsupported claim MUST be removed, narrowed, researched further, or marked unknown.
The context gate MUST evaluate:
The gate MUST fail when a missing or unsupported item could materially change the thesis, factual risk, artifact type, or legitimate speaking position.
The gate MUST NOT pass because the implementation can produce fluent text.
The implementation MUST define a reader promise describing what the audience should understand, know, feel, or be able to do.
Content design MUST include:
The design MUST follow the selected format and topic without forcing optional template elements.
The media decision MUST state:
Drafting MUST begin only when a valid `context-ready` gate record, current content design, and current media decision exist. The active state at that point is `media-decided`.
The draft MUST:
The implementation MUST perform passes appropriate to:
Edits MUST NOT remove necessary uncertainty, disclosure, context, or source boundaries merely to improve flow.
Before generation or commissioning, every selected visual MUST have:
Generated imagery MUST NOT be presented as documentary evidence.
The implementation MUST retain generation provenance required by task, law, contract, platform, or profile.
The implementation MUST execute RFC-0005 against the edited text and selected visual assets.
Review MUST use one frozen artifact revision per pass. Required reviewers MUST complete or return an input failure.
The implementation MUST:
The pipeline MUST NOT label an artifact publication-ready solely because a draft exists.
A ready task MUST return or retain separable parts:
Exact serialization MAY differ. Publication copy MUST remain distinguishable from internal notes.
A blocked record MUST identify:
Resumption MUST validate that pinned sources, registries, task constraints, and completed artifacts remain current. A material change MUST invalidate affected downstream stages.
A conforming implementation MUST retain enough information to identify:
Each material source SHOULD have a source record containing:
A claim ledger SHOULD contain:
The body SHOULD be meaning-complete before the implementation optimizes title, lead, deck, excerpt, tags, or visual copy.

Exact documentary appearance, verified data, product interfaces, medical anatomy, maps, technical labels, code, and historical records SHOULD use verified assets or manually reviewed construction rather than unconstrained generation.
Every runtime object MUST have one stable `id`.
- MUST be unique within a specification revision;
- MUST NOT be reused for a semantically different object;
- MUST remain unchanged when only the title, prose, or repository path changes.

An object MUST use the narrowest kind matching its responsibility. A platform object MUST NOT encode a universal evidence rule. A tone object MUST NOT create author authority. A topic object SHOULD NOT prescribe a fixed article structure unless the structure is necessary to preserve domain meaning.
A runtime object record MUST contain:
Missing optional arrays MUST be interpreted as empty arrays. An empty applicability array means “not restricted by this selector,” not “applicable nowhere.”
- MUST be relative to the repository root;
- MUST NOT be absolute;
- MUST NOT contain `..` path traversal;
- MUST resolve to one file;
- MUST be unique among runtime objects;
Moving a file without changing its semantics MUST preserve the object ID and MUST update the registry atomically.
Each runtime Markdown module MUST begin with frontmatter containing at least:
The frontmatter `id`, `kind`, and `status` MUST equal the registry values. Human-readable prose outside frontmatter MUST NOT redefine those values.
Additional frontmatter MAY be used when a validator understands or safely ignores it. Required machine metadata MUST live in the registry rather than only in prose.
- A resolver MUST reject an explicitly selected object when a non-empty selector excludes the task value.
- MUST reference known object IDs;
- MUST NOT contain self-dependencies;
- MUST NOT contain cycles;
- MUST load dependencies before dependants;
- MUST preserve transitive dependencies;
An object MUST NOT depend on a narrower object unless that narrower scope is required for every valid use of the dependant.
For example, `platform.telegram.foundation` MAY require `platform.social.foundation`. `topic.general.foundation` MUST NOT require every specialist topic.
- MUST map a public configuration value to one known object of the matching kind;
- MUST use unique value IDs and module IDs within the index;
- MUST NOT map two values to the same module unless the alias behavior is explicitly documented;
- MUST remain consistent with the object's applicability selector.
- MUST retain its ID;
- MUST NOT be selected by default for new configurations;
Every potentially breaking change MUST include migration notes before release.
Community or vendor extensions SHOULD use a documented namespace when collision is possible. An extension MUST NOT use a core ID for different behavior.
An extension proposal MUST document:
A conforming object validator MUST detect:
Validation failure MUST produce a non-success result and identify the affected file or object.
Object paths and index values are untrusted input to tooling. Resolvers MUST prevent path traversal and MUST NOT execute module content as code merely because it is registered.
An object MAY contain sensitive guidance but MUST NOT embed private source material, credentials, tokens, or proprietary content without authorization.
- SHOULD follow `<kind-or-domain>.<name>[.<variant>]`;
- SHOULD remain stable when practical, but path stability is weaker than ID stability.
- SHOULD avoid dependencies that exist only for prose convenience.
- SHOULD declare a fallback only when fallback semantics are defined by RFC-0004;
RFCs SHOULD be listed in a separate RFC index because normative-document dependency is not runtime module dependency.
- SHOULD identify its replacement in prose or migration metadata;
Resolution MUST:
Resolution MUST NOT attempt to improve prose. It prepares the instruction context for RFC-0002.
The resolver MUST distinguish:
It MUST preserve the origin of every resolved axis.
1. MUST preserve the original input value in the audit record;
3. MUST NOT fuzzy-match an unknown stable ID or public value;
4. MUST NOT translate a public value into a semantically similar value without an explicit alias;
5. MUST validate the pinned registry revision before resolution.
For example, `science` MAY map to `topic.science.foundation` because the topic index declares it. `scientific` MUST NOT map automatically unless an index declares that alias.
Every Editorial Core resolution MUST include:
An implementation MAY add a specialist reviewer required by a selected extension. It MUST record the reason.
- A known explicit topic MUST map through the topic index.
- A high-risk or materially specialist topic MUST NOT silently fall back to general when doing so would weaken evidence or safety requirements.
- If content type is absent and the task can safely inherit the platform default, the resolver MAY infer it and MUST record the inference.
- If an explicit content type conflicts with a non-empty platform format selector, the resolver MUST return an applicability error.
- A platform default MUST NOT determine topic, skill, tone, or author perspective.
- An explicit known skill MUST be loaded.
- An unknown skill MUST produce an error.
- A resolver MUST NOT select a skill merely because its example resembles the requested subject.
Multiple skills MAY be loaded only when their jobs are materially required and compatible. The resolver MUST record the primary skill.
Tone MAY be inferred when the audience, platform, and task establish a low-risk default. The inference MUST be recorded.

Author perspective MUST NOT be inferred as first-person or expert solely from tone, platform, or topic. If legitimate perspective is unknown and would materially affect the artifact, resolution MAY complete but RFC-0002 context gating MUST fail.
Dependencies MUST load before dependants.
Load order MUST NOT silently become a substitute for normative precedence. Conflict handling follows RFC-0001.
- A conversational tone MAY change phrasing but MUST NOT weaken a health disclaimer.
- A Telegram module MAY change paragraphing but MUST NOT remove a scientific limitation.
A failed resolution MUST return a machine-distinguishable code and human-readable context.
An error MUST identify the affected value or object. The resolver MUST NOT continue with a silent partial module set when a required root or dependency fails.
A successful resolution MUST emit or retain:
Exact serialization MAY differ, but the semantics MUST be preserved.
The resolver SHOULD choose the narrowest topic controlling the material claims.
- When no skill accurately describes the task, the resolver SHOULD omit the skill.
When multiple valid topological orders exist, an implementation SHOULD use a deterministic order, such as:
Implementations SHOULD expose unused explicitly requested modules as warnings or errors rather than loading them without effect.
A conforming review process MUST:

One implementation MAY execute several roles, but it MUST preserve each role's scope and findings separately. A combined reviewer MUST NOT omit a required checklist merely because another role appears to cover it.

Every review run MUST identify:
A reviewer MUST return an input error rather than guess when a missing item prevents evaluation within its scope.
Each finding MUST contain:
Exact serialization MAY differ, but the fields and semantics MUST remain recoverable.
Severity MUST reflect impact, not correction effort. An easy-to-fix false claim may still be a blocker.

`accepted-risk` MUST NOT change a claim classification or make an unsupported claim verified. An artifact with an accepted-risk blocker or major finding MUST NOT claim unqualified publication-ready status under this specification.
Review MAY be parallelized when reviewers use the same frozen artifact revision. Findings from different revisions MUST NOT be merged without identifying the revision boundary.
Aggregation MUST NOT average severities into a lower category.
A revision MUST:
Every fixed blocker or major finding MUST be verified.

When a visual is produced, review MUST compare:
The visual reviewer MUST recommend omission when an optional asset cannot be made truthful, useful, accessible, or authorized.
An artifact MAY be `ready-with-minor-findings` when only minor findings or notes remain and the publisher accepts them. The review report MUST preserve them.
The report MUST include:
Review notes MUST remain separate from public copy unless disclosure or platform context requires publication.

Reviewers MUST receive only the source material required for their scope. Review reports MUST NOT expose private source content, credentials, hidden personal data, or confidential prompts without authorization.
A reviewer SHOULD evaluate an artifact from the supplied task and evidence record rather than from the draft author's hidden rationale.
For high-risk tasks, implementations SHOULD use a distinct review pass or independent evaluator when practical.
Duplicate findings SHOULD be linked to one issue rather than counted as independent evidence of severity.
A revision SHOULD NOT rewrite the entire artifact when a local correction is sufficient.
Every case MUST include:
A case MUST NOT contain invented sources or hidden facts used to penalize an output.
Mutable sources MUST be pinned, archived when permitted, or accompanied by enough identity and retrieval metadata to reproduce the evidence boundary.
The snapshot MUST preserve:
Private or licensed sources MUST NOT be published in a benchmark package without authorization. The benchmark MAY publish hashes, metadata, or an access procedure instead.
When a benchmark claims an effect from Human Writing Rules, arms MUST keep these values equal unless the benchmark explicitly studies them:
The intended treatment difference MUST be stated precisely.
A baseline MUST be credible for the tested workflow. It MUST NOT be intentionally crippled to exaggerate improvement.

Runs MUST NOT be discarded merely because they weaken the desired result.
Evaluation MUST score:

An evaluator MUST NOT penalize a correct `none` decision for lacking visual polish. A required visual that cannot be produced or reviewed is a blocked or failed run, not an implicit zero-quality image unless the rubric defines that failure.
Each run MUST preserve:
Secrets and private chain-of-thought MUST NOT be required for benchmark reproduction. An implementation SHOULD preserve observable decisions and artifacts instead.
A high average score MUST NOT erase a hard failure.
Evaluation instructions MUST define:
Human comparison SHOULD be blinded to arm identity when practical. Evaluators MUST NOT be told the desired winner.
An automated reviewer MAY supplement human evaluation. It MUST NOT be described as independent human evidence.
Aggregation MUST retain case and dimension detail.
Small samples MUST be labeled exploratory. Statistical inference MUST state its assumptions and method.

Conclusions MUST remain within the tested:
Historical results MUST remain associated with the exact case and specification revision used. Re-running a changed case MUST NOT silently replace previous results.

Benchmark packages MUST remove credentials and unauthorized personal or confidential material. Visual assets, source snapshots, prompts, and outputs MUST retain copyright, trademark, likeness, and license restrictions.
Generative outputs vary. A comparative claim SHOULD use repeated runs across more than one case and, when possible, more than one model or execution date.
